description:
Per RFC 8621 §1.3 (lines 260, 350, 408):
- Identity/* and EmailSubmission/* require `urn:ietf:params:jmap:submission`
- VacationResponse/* requires `urn:ietf:params:jmap:vacationresponse`
- Mail/* (Email, Mailbox, Thread, SearchSnippet) requires
  `urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail`

Current code (`src/methods/mod.rs:321`) defines exactly one constant:
```
const USING_MAIL: &[&str] = &["urn:ietf:params:jmap:core",
                              "urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail"];
```
and every method in identity.rs, submission.rs, and vacation.rs builds its
request with `super::build_request(method, args, super::USING_MAIL)`.

Per RFC 8620 §3.3: "Servers MUST NOT use methods from a capability that is
not declared in the request's `using` field." A strict server rejects every
Identity/*, EmailSubmission/*, and VacationResponse/* call this crate makes
with `unknownCapability` or `unknownMethod`.

Most lenient servers will accept anyway (Stalwart, Cyrus often do), but the
client is non-conformant and any spec-following server (or a future Stalwart
release that tightens) will fail.

Fix: add `USING_SUBMISSION` and `USING_VACATION` constants and route each
method through the right one. The submission constant must include
`urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail` AND `urn:ietf:params:jmap:submission` because
EmailSubmission references emailId / threadId (mail-typed fields) and the
onSuccessUpdateEmail mechanism produces an implicit Email/set invocation
on the same request.

Wiremock smoke tests do not currently assert on the `using` array — add
assertions while fixing.

Canonical-template: every extension-client sibling cookie-cut from this
crate will have the same pattern. Audit/fix in lockstep.
title: Identity/EmailSubmission/VacationResponse methods send wrong 'using' capability set
